correctness.rationale: Define the zero-sum Euclidean dual Lipschitz ball for every integer p>=3 and q>=2. Its edge root projections have squared lengths (2,0,0) on a clique edge and ((p-1)/p,(q-1)/q,N/(pq)) on a cross edge. The displayed S is positive and all its edge slab supports are <=1, with the stated equality conditions. Explicit nonnegative normalized per-edge conductances give a Laplacian L with eigenvalues pv+qw, pw, Nw and identity dLS=I_H. For any translated inscribed ellipsoid y+E(T), the opposite-slab bounds imply tr(LT)<=1, hence det(T)<=d^{-d}/det(L)=det(S) by AM-GM; equality requires T=S and y=0 because positive-weight cross roots span H. Comparison to the cross-only bipartite design establishes the exact if-and-only-if q>=p+1. The full proof is in RESULT.md. The standalone exact Fraction checker passed 342 cases, including 42 complete ambient matrix identities; these finite tests are corroborative, not the proof.

The historical split-graph interior covariance does not determine the John ellipsoid. value.rationale: Determining a canonical extremal ellipsoid for an infinite family of finite-dimensional Lipschitz-free dual Banach balls is a motivated natural geometric invariant. The graph addition of binomial(p,2) genuine edges has no effect on that ellipsoid exactly for q>=p+1, while true clique-facet nontangency begins only for q>=p+2, separating two distinct structural transitions. Unlike a single example or routine normalized scalar, this is a complete two-parameter contact classification, exact spectrum and intrinsic volume; general D-optimal design theorems do not supply the evaluated thresholds without new casework.
